details: 28 Oct, spec-met (a-spec-fix-is-marked-met-by-reading-not-by-runni): the rule 'the checker runs a sketch of a runnable failing case' could not be proven in 7 paid bench runs ($2.83): graders read only the final reply, the workspace and the ledger (agent starts, tool names, no commands), so 'a script ran' is graded by words in the reply ('sketch|scratch|script|скрипт'). Run 6 (rule on) found the defect by reading and the word grader failed; runs 4-5 (rule off) gave the same verdicts. details: CONFIRMED on real data. tool_calls reads message.content of every JSON line whatever its `type`; Claude Code subagent
transcripts now hold `type: api-request-blob` lines (keys agentId, hash, sessionId, type) whose message repeats the tool_use
(same id, the command as sent, e.g. with a hook's `cd <ws> &&` prefix). The count field, the "N of M" note and the llm
grader's tool list are all doubled. The test fixture has no such lines, so the tests pass while real data is wrong.
Size: 15 minutes (keep the first tool_use per id, or read only type == "assistant" lines; add a blob line to the fixture).
evidence: python over the subagent file, per tool_use line: "13 assistant ... tooluse cKxw7dQe Bash relay check show ..." then
"18 api-request-blob ... tooluse cKxw7dQe Bash cd /Users/amidman/.relay/bench/2026-10-2..." (same for all 5 ids).
rb.tool_called({"input": r"\bpython3?\b", "count": 2}, sid, calls) -> (True, '2 of 13 calls matched: Bash python3 -I -c ...')
failing_case: Real run ~/.relay/bench/2026-10-28T06-07-08Z, session 7e59b0c6-b48f-4b55-b026-35f262a817c2. Its checker subagent made 5 tool
calls (5 tool_use ids, 5 tool_results), of which 1 ran python. tool_calls() returns 13 (3 main + 10 subagent), because each
`assistant` line is followed by an `api-request-blob` line carrying the same tool_use id. A grader
{input = '\bpython3?\b', count = 2} passes ("2 of 13 calls matched") with one python call; it should fail ("1 of 8").
fix_hint: In tool_calls, dedupe by block["id"] (keep the first, or prefer the blob's input if the hook-rewritten command is wanted),

2. Two distinct tool_use ids both running python: count=2 passes.
4. Re-grading run 06-07-08Z gives 8 calls in total, not 13.

details: CONFIRMED on real data (tool_result flags printed for that run). tool_calls reads only tool_use blocks and ignores the matching
tool_result, so a refused call (PreToolUse hook deny, permission refusal) is indistinguishable from one that ran. In bench runs
the relay guards do refuse calls (guard-main.sh refused 2 of 5 checker calls in this run), so it is reachable on ordinary use.
Size: 15-30 minutes (map tool_use_id -> tool_result, drop calls whose result is an error starting with "PreToolUse:" or a
evidence: tool_result scan of the subagent file: "Bash is_error= True PreToolUse:Bash hook error: [.../guard-main.sh]: gu..."
"Write is_error= True PreToolUse:Write hook error: ..."; main file: "Agent is_error= True PreToolUse:Agent hook error: Routing: ..."
rb.tool_called({"input": r"cat > \.review/spec-check\.md"}, sid, calls)[0] -> True; Write grader -> True
failing_case: Same real run 06-07-08Z: the checker's `cat > .review/spec-check.md <<'EOF' ...` Bash call and its Write were refused by
guard-main.sh (tool_result is_error=true, "PreToolUse:Bash hook error: ... guard-main.sh"). tool_called({input='cat > \.review/spec-check\.md'})
and tool_called({tool='^Write$', input='spec-check'}) both pass now; they should fail, the command never ran. Likewise the main
session's first Agent call (refused by the routing hook) counts as an agent call. The item's promise is "a Bash call ran python"
as a fact; a python call blocked by a guard would pass it.
fix_hint: Collect tool_result blocks (user lines) by tool_use_id in the same pass; skip a tool_use whose result is_error and whose text
starts with "PreToolUse:" (hook block) or is a permission refusal. Fixture: add one blocked call.
pass_cases: 1. Transcript: tool_use T1 Bash "python3 s.py" with a tool_result T1 is_error=true content "PreToolUse:Bash hook error: blocked": {input='python3'} fails.
2. tool_use T2 Bash "python3 s.py" with tool_result is_error=true content "Exit code 1 ..." (it ran, failed): {input='python3'} passes.
3. tool_use T3 with a normal tool_result: passes (as today).
4. tool_use with no tool_result yet (last line of a cut-off run): decide and test one way (counted as attempted is acceptable if documented).

details: CONFIRMED by reading (_SECRET_NAME against the names exported in the owner's shell; values never read). The queue item's pass
case is "No secret from the environment appears in what graders read"; a database URL with a password is such a secret, and
the bench copies os.environ to the session, so the agent can see and use it. Reachable only when an agent writes the literal
value into a command, hence MEDIUM, not HIGH. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: grep -ho '^ *export NAME' ~/.zshrc ... (names only): ... CLIENT_BACK_POSTGRES_DEV_DATASOURCE ... SORM_DWH_DATASOURCE SORM_DWH_USER GLONASS_KUBE_LOGIN ...
failing_case: The owner's ~/.zshrc exports (names only read) CLIENT_BACK_POSTGRES_PROD_DATASOURCE, SORM_DWH_DATASOURCE, SORM_DWH_USER,
GLONASS_KUBE_LOGIN and nine more *_POSTGRES_*_DATASOURCE; none matches KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|CREDENTIAL|AUTH.
A bench session that runs `psql "<the literal postgres://user:pass@host/db value>"` puts the password into tool_calls, the
tool_called note (results.json, report.md) and the llm grader prompt unredacted. Should be "[redacted]".
fix_hint: Add DATASOURCE|DSN|LOGIN|PASS|PRIVATE|CONN to the name list, and redact any env value that looks like a URL with userinfo
(re ://[^/\s:@]+:[^/\s@]+@) whatever its name. One more test with a fake DATASOURCE value.
pass_cases: 1. env FAKE_PG_DATASOURCE="postgres://u:s3cretpass@h/db", a Bash call containing that value: no call, note or llm prompt contains it.
2. env FAKE_BENCH_API_KEY (the existing test) still redacted.
3. env HOME / PATH-like values (no secret-looking name) are not redacted, so `python3 /Users/x/scratch.py` still matches.
4. A value of the form scheme://user:pass@host in any env var is redacted whatever its name.
